title: Use short and long instead of gshort and glong
description:
Remove a check for G_HAVE_GLONG_DOUBLE, which appears to have never
existed.

Ping #19116

notes.body: assigned to @geraldcombs

> Remove a check for G_HAVE_GLONG_DOUBLE, which appears to have never existed.

`long double` dates back to C90 (and I'd probably find it in my dead-tree C89, if I still had it).

But, if they didn't bother with `glongdouble` because it wasn't necessary, why did they bother with `gshort`, `glong`, etc.?

I believe that `guchar`, `gushort`, `gulong`, etc. were all with the intention of making various macro substitutions easier by avoiding having multiple tokens for a type name, and then they ended up including the other ones "for completeness" https://docs.gtk.org/glib/types.html

Doesn't answer the question of why no `long double` equivalent - though there is `gfloat` and `gdouble` which are used in a small number of places in the codebase.
resolved all threads

"This type [glong] only exists for symmetry with gulong."

"gulong can be used in contexts where a type name must be a single word, such as in the GType name of G_TYPE_ULONG or when generating a family of function names for multiple types using macros."

This should probably be an `int` - not that it matters, as the return value isn't ever checked!

See !15136, which makes it an int *and* adds XXX comments before all the calls to `c_warn_int()`.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/15133/diffs?diff_id=973192350&start_sha=62ab5ef17b19ade7bc2ca19e791b5c548d0ed01a#23f185f5a6e73f0b37cac9f5f72d8b534f997d54_1739_1739)
OK, I backed out this change in favor of !15136.
I'm not sure why this is a (g)short, but it looks as if it should be a `guint8` - it's used to hold a value between 0 and 255.
Fixed.
Same with these two.
Fixed.
And this one, too.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/15133/diffs?diff_id=973192350&start_sha=62ab5ef17b19ade7bc2ca19e791b5c548d0ed01a#1f5223fdcd892937a8193c1ce3c3d6a0713d47b9_733_733)
Switched to an int since it's used for offset calculations.
This is a two-byte signed value, according to [MS-TDS], so it probably should be a `gint16` or a `int16_t`.
Fixed.

Sadly, this is one of those places where the GLib developers made a weird data type choice - it probably *should* have been either a `gsize` or a `gssize`, but there's another place in GLib where they made the same mistake, which is something you can probably get away with on UN\*Xes, as all the UN\*Xes supported by GLib are either ILP32 or LP64, but sucks on Windows, which uses LLP64.

So maybe this one should remain a `glong`, the ugliness of which is, in this context, a feature, reflecting the ugliness of the choice of data type by the GLib developers.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/15133/diffs?diff_id=973192350&start_sha=62ab5ef17b19ade7bc2ca19e791b5c548d0ed01a#51ca6cd053ee277302ea1df9bd4030f29b20ee7d_350_350)
I switched it back. This is our last glong, so I removed that conversion from convert-glib-types.py.

> "gulong can be used in contexts where a type name must be a single word, such as in the GType name of G_TYPE_ULONG ..."

Presumably there's a reason why the GType name could not have been G_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG.

commits_data.title: Switch away from gshort and glong
commits_data.message:
Switch away from gshort and glong

Switch from gshort to more appropriate types in the IPDC and TDS
dissectors. Remove a check for G_HAVE_GLONG_DOUBLE, which appears to
have never existed.

We don't want automatically convert glongs any more, so remove the glong
conversion in convert-glib-types.py.

Ping #19116
